overview.summary: DevOps engineers connect software development and operations, building the tools and systems that let teams release software quickly and keep it running reliably.
overview.problems: They automate repeated tasks, reduce human error and help teams release updates safely.
overview.worksWith: Software developers, testers, security teams, system administrators and product managers.
overview.workplaces: Technology companies, banks, start-ups and other organizations that run software, often remotely or in offices.

timeline.title: Check system health
timeline.description: The engineer looks at dashboards and alerts for problems overnight.
timeline.why: Many services must be available all day.

timeline.title: Automating tasks
timeline.description: The engineer writes scripts and configuration that build, test and release software automatically.
timeline.why: Automation reduces mistakes and saves time.

timeline.title: Helping developers
timeline.description: The engineer fixes failures in the release pipeline, answers questions and improves tools.
timeline.why: Developers work faster when their tools work well.

timeline.title: Improving reliability and security
timeline.description: The engineer updates systems, adds monitoring and reviews who has access to what.
timeline.why: Preventing problems is better than fixing them.

timeline.title: Documentation and planning
timeline.description: The engineer writes instructions and plans upgrades.
timeline.why: Clear notes help the whole team and future colleagues.

timeline.title: On-call and incidents
timeline.description: When a service fails, the team investigates and restores it, sometimes at night.
timeline.why: Users depend on services being available.

responsibilities: Building and maintaining automated release pipelines
Monitoring systems and responding to problems
challenges: On-call duty can interrupt evenings and weekends.
Small configuration mistakes can cause big outages.
Many technologies have to be learned at once.
Pressure is high when services fail and users are affected.
Speed of release has to be balanced with safety.
The work is often invisible: people notice when things break, not when they work.
workEnvironment: Mostly desk and computer based, in offices or remotely, working closely with developers. Work includes steady build time, meetings and, in some teams, on-call rotations. Hours are often regular, but incidents can change them.
rewards: Making teams faster and systems more reliable
tradeoffs: Being invisible when things go well
Titles and pay that vary by country and employer

activity.title: Automate a boring task on your own computer
steps: Pick a repeated task, such as sorting downloaded files into folders by type.
Follow a free beginner tutorial for a simple script in a language such as Python.
Run the script only on a copy of a folder you made yourself and compare the time with doing it by hand.
activity.outcome: You practise breaking a task into steps and automating it, which is the core idea of DevOps.
activity.safety: Test only on copies of your own files, never run scripts from unknown sources, and do not change system settings or use administrator access without an adult.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
